Q: How to use an HTML # anchor in a dynamic URL A:

Your use of the anchor in a dynamic URL is correct. The syntax is:

[page]?[query]#[fragment]

Example: Open the "Egypt" Wikipedia page at the "Geography" heading.

Solution:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt?#Geography

What is happening?

  1. The query, not including the fragment, is sent to the server, resulting in the "Egypt" page being sent back to the client for rendering.
  2. The client browser now processes the fragment by finding the tag with the id attribute having the value Geography and scrolls down to it.

You will notice that the page source contains:
<h2 id="Geography">Geography</h2>

Why your code does not work?
The snippet of code you have shown is correct and the error is likely not due to this. We cannot offer you help if you don't show us any errors, screenshots or the full page.php code. However, your statement about the duplicate content may be a clue:

I am redirected to page.php which has its content repeated vertically.

Q: Error in Python: missing 1 required positional argument A:

When you declare your function you do this :

def demand_curve(c,Q,y,pb):
    ...

So you have four parameters c, Q, y and pb, later in the code you call it using :

demand_curve(Q_num, 50, 2)

So in the way you call it you have

  • c = Q_num
  • Q = 50
  • y = 2
  • pb = Nothing at all

And python don't like this so you should provide and additional value when you call this function or provide a default value for the last parameter for example :

def demand_curve(c,Q,y,pb = "a default value"):
    ...

Q: Which services are typically required to scale a LAMP stack for high-traffic production environments? A:

Thanks for the suggestion.

I agree that with OPcache enabled, PHP itself is rarely the primary bottleneck in typical LAMP applications, and that optimizing the application and database layer should come first.

Regarding Swoole, it looks interesting, although it seems to move away from the traditional LAMP execution model. In that sense, I’m currently more focused on understanding when additional infrastructure components (like caching layers or reverse proxies) become necessary within a standard LAMP architecture.

Q: Spring Boot requestMatchers permitAll always return 403 A:

I saw a comment about removing server.servlet.context-path=/api from application.properties. That is correct, I thought it was worth adding a bit more of explaination since the question is still open

When you set a context path, Spring Boot prepends /api to all endpoints, but your security configuration still looks for the original paths. So /api/user/test becomes /api/api/user/test

A good way to fix it is to remove context-path, but if you want it because you want all the requests to be preprended by /api, then you can keep it, but you'll have to update your security configuration and your controller to have path /user/test instead of /api/user/test
